html:
Eyring is a city in Dangar named after the family that owns it. On the author’s map, a note beside it reads “the ancestral seat of those very von Eyrings”—a reference to chapter 17, where Dietrich, learning that his cover story makes him Katrina von Eyring’s cousin, asks whether these are the Eyrings after whom the city is named. “The city is their hereditary possession,” Olkha replies.

The von Eyring family (ch. 17, 25, 29, 31)

The Eyrings are an ancient and powerful family. Prince Lenz is told that killing Lieutenant von Eyring over a trivial matter would earn him influential enemies at court, especially if the killer were a foreigner (ch. 25). In their cover story, Dietrich and Katrina are cousins from a cadet branch of the family. Its head is Margrave Maximian von Eyring, a miser who nonetheless protects his own (ch. 29); in chapter 31, the calling cards of Count Ludwig von Lurd and Margrave von Eyring help secure Dietrich’s release from the gendarmerie. The city itself is not described in the text.
